question: Can a frozen autoregressive video world model preserve both temporal coherence and the appearance of revisited scenes beyond its trained context by giving a fixed-size compressed KV cache stable, in-distribution RoPE addresses and content-aware memory writers?

key_findings.claim: Long-horizon cache failure has separable addressability and content-corruption components, so retaining old keys is not sufficient.
key_findings.evidence: For MG2-1.3B, temporal query-key offsets beyond the trained maximum of five latent frames push fast RoPE components into unseen phases; at an illustrative offset of 30, the three fastest pairs exceed 3π. Independently, averaging already rotated keys mixes distinct phases and can cancel their signal. The paper's frequency analysis and mean-score proposition explain why canonicalizing keys before aggregation avoids the latter failure.

key_findings.claim: WorldTrace makes an arbitrary fixed number of summaries individually readable at any rollout horizon by assigning positions from cache-slot rank rather than source time.
key_findings.evidence: Each summary slot s is read at q-(L_attn-1-s), which stays inside the trained offset range and remains distinct as q advances. Source keys are first unrotated to canonical coordinates and then freshly rotated to that virtual slot, separating stored content from its original timestamp.

key_findings.claim: With content compression fixed, horizon-stable slot-rank addressing improves coherence over capped or horizon-dependent positions.
key_findings.evidence: Using canonical averaging in every arm, WorldTrace reaches TempSSIM 0.413 and 0.545 at N=8 and N=16, versus 0.390/0.530 for Block-relative and 0.377/0.479 for Centroid-linear. At N=48 in the longer coherence panel, WorldTrace-Field scores 0.545 versus 0.472 for sliding-window caching, a 15.5% relative gain, and has the lowest reported Local Scene Drift, 0.0295 versus 0.0305.

key_findings.claim: Canonical-space averaging reduces phase-cancellation error, but the Field writer is a coherence mechanism rather than a strong episodic-recall mechanism.
key_findings.evidence: At N=16 and four summary slots, canonical averaging reduces LatentDiff from 0.312 to 0.233 relative to averaging rotated keys. Yet on the long ABA recall sweep, WorldTrace-Field remains in the compression-only tier, scoring PAC 0.602 at N=256, close to the sliding-window score 0.631 and far below verbatim landmarks at 0.989.

key_findings.claim: Verbatim scene-entry landmarks substantially improve revisit fidelity over a sliding window across several controlled loop geometries, while gains become small for the hardest full-pan condition.
key_findings.evidence: On ABA at N=16, WorldTrace-Landmark raises PAC from 0.723±0.013 to 0.864±0.009, a 19.5% relative improvement; it also raises PAC from 0.673 to 0.792 on ABCA and from 0.666 to 0.799 on ABCDA. It improves every reported LoopBench condition, but the 360-degree pan gain is only 0.018 absolute, 0.577 versus 0.559.

key_findings.claim: The landmark result transfers to a second, much larger backbone, whereas Field averaging adds little when camera conditioning already supplies a recall signal.
key_findings.evidence: On the 14B LingBot-World backbone, landmarks improve PAC over sliding-window retention by 8.9%, 14.1%, and 7.3% at 4×, 6×, and 8× training horizon, with no significant gain at 2×. WorldTrace-Field remains within 0.005 of the baseline at 4× and is only modestly above it at the other horizons.

key_findings.claim: The attended cache and per-step GPU cost stay bounded, but the primary Field writer moves an O(T) history burden to host memory; a streaming writer removes that burden with a small quality tradeoff.
key_findings.evidence: At N=64/256/512, the recompute Field writer matches sliding-window peak GPU memory exactly, while retaining 5.4 MB of canonical keys per evicted latent frame in host memory. Its streaming alternative uses constant writer state and scores TempSSIM 0.606/0.538 at N=32/48, versus 0.613/0.545 for recomputation and 0.571/0.472 for sliding-window caching. All methods remain within 6% of the baseline wall-clock time per chunk in the reported short-horizon runtime test.

method.core_idea: Treat a compressed video KV cache as two coupled design problems: an address must remain inside the frozen model's trained positional distribution, and a writer must retain the kind of history future queries will need.
method.mechanism: Split the six-frame MG2 attention budget into recent verbatim slots and distant summary slots. Read every summary at a unique slot-rank-relative temporal position. Store keys in unrotated canonical coordinates and re-rotate them only when read. WorldTrace-Field uniformly averages contiguous historical groups for smooth continuation; WorldTrace-Landmark detects canonical-key cosine-distance spikes and preserves the most recent scene-entry frames verbatim. LoopBench drives the model away from and back to its own earlier view and scores pose-aligned return frames against that generated reference.
assumptions: The frozen generator is autoregressive, uses temporal RoPE on keys, and exposes a known local training-time attention range.
Future continuation queries distribute attention smoothly within temporal groups when Field averaging is used.
Recall queries concentrate on one of at most N_s detected scene-entry frames when landmarks are used.
Canonical-key cosine discontinuities are a usable geometry-free proxy for scene entry.
Reassigning old content to a recent virtual slot is less harmful than asking the model to extrapolate to an unseen absolute offset.
Position-Aligned CLIP and consecutive-frame SSIM are adequate proxies for spatial recall and temporal coherence in the controlled camera paths.

techniques.role: Assigns every summary a distinct fixed relative offset inside the trained temporal range, independent of rollout length.
Removes source-time RoPE phase before compression and applies one fresh rotation at the current virtual address.
Represents a bounded cache as a row-stochastic projection from the full history, exposing averaging and one-hot retention as two choices of the same operator.
Compresses old frames into uniform temporal groups to favor group-level coherence.
Uses spikes in canonical-key cosine distance to retain sparse verbatim scene traces for later recall.
Caches one canonical landmark key and re-rotates from that source each time, avoiding repeated BF16 unrotate-rerotate drift.
Creates navigation loops whose first visit supplies the reference for scoring a later revisit without an external target video.
Maintains per-slot sums and counts with exact bucket merges so Field writer state can remain constant in horizon.

evaluations.setting: MG2-1.3B, canonical averaging held fixed, N=8 and N=16 rollouts
MG2-1.3B open-ended coherence rollouts, N=32 and N=48
evaluations.result: WorldTrace-Field scores 0.613/0.0250 at N=32 and 0.545/0.0295 at N=48

evaluations.setting: LoopBench on 100 initial scenes per condition, varying topology, horizon, camera pan, and revisit pattern
evaluations.result: Landmarks improve PAC in every reported condition, including 0.864 versus 0.723 on ABA N=16
WorldTrace-Landmark reaches 0.989 at N=256; canonical-K anchoring reaches 0.610 and WorldTrace-Field 0.602

evaluations.setting: MG2-1.3B memory and runtime audit on one A100 80GB
evaluations.metric: Peak GPU memory and seconds per AR chunk
evaluations.result: Field matches baseline GPU memory; Field/Landmark take 0.99/1.00 seconds versus 0.95 seconds per chunk

limitations: Author-stated: the intervention cannot improve motion, per-chunk visual quality, or action following inherited from the frozen backbone.
Author-stated: the method assumes an autoregressive generator with temporal RoPE and a known local attention window; it does not directly apply to other positional systems or architectures.
Author-stated: Field summaries become progressively lossier because each slot averages roughly T/N_s frames and therefore blurs frame-level scene detail.
Author-stated: landmark recall succeeds only when the detector stores the right scene, and at most N_s distinct landmarks survive oldest-first eviction.
Author-stated: the projection near-optimality statements are conditional definitions for two query families under a relaxed objective; the paper does not measure those conditions on the frozen model.

Reviewer-identified: the main recompute Field writer has linearly growing host-memory state, so the headline fixed-memory property applies to the GPU attention cache, not the complete system; the streaming variant is the truly horizon-constant writer.
Reviewer-identified: most evidence comes from one 1.3B game world model, with one smaller cross-architecture table on a 14B model; there is no broad model, environment, or action-policy study.

Reviewer-identified: LoopBench compares a return against the model's own earlier generation, so it measures self-consistency rather than correctness against persistent external world state, and CLIP similarity may miss object identity or geometric errors.

Reviewer-identified: WorldTrace-Field is not uniformly better on both coherence metrics or recall; at N=32 its Scene Drift is worse than sliding window, and several mixed Field/Landmark allocations fall below baseline.
failure_modes: A gradual scene transition may never cross the cosine threshold, while a harmless lighting or motion discontinuity may consume a landmark slot.
More than N_s relevant places evict old landmarks, so long tours or branching environments can forget a location before revisit.
A virtual slot discards the source frame's true temporal distance; queries whose dynamics depend on elapsed time can misinterpret the relocated content.
Canonical averaging reduces key norm as heterogeneous sources cancel, which can underweight distant summaries after softmax even though their mean pre-softmax score is preserved at a shared position.
Uniform temporal groups blur rare but important events, while verbatim landmarks sacrifice the broad context needed for smooth continuation.
The recompute writer can become host-memory- or transfer-bound on extremely long rollouts despite constant GPU attention state.

Pose-aligned CLIP can reward semantically similar but geometrically wrong return frames, and using an earlier generated frame as reference can preserve the model's own artifact rather than a true scene.
Backbones whose camera-conditioning signal dominates cache reads may gain little from Field summaries, as the LingBot result already suggests.
reusable_insights: Audit memory addressability separately from memory content; a retained value is useless if the frozen reader only sees it at an out-of-distribution address.
Compress position-dependent representations only after mapping them into a position-neutral coordinate system.
Expose memory policies through a common projection interface so dense summaries, sparse exemplars, and learned mixtures can be compared under one budget.
Evaluate long-term generative memory with explicit leave-and-return interventions, not only adjacent-frame smoothness or generic video quality.
Report memory outside the accelerator cache as well as GPU allocation; offloading can hide horizon-dependent system state.
Use separate writers for distributed context and episodic recall because one averaging rule is unlikely to serve both query distributions.
Include difficult cases where the proposed memory should not help, such as short horizons or strong pose-conditioned backbones, to locate the actual bottleneck.
open_questions: Can a learned streaming projection interpolate between Field and Landmark rows while remaining stable under a frozen model's attention distribution?
Can revisit likelihood, action history, and camera geometry drive landmark replacement without requiring backbone fine-tuning?
How should virtual positions encode both addressability and coarse elapsed time when future dynamics depend on temporal distance?
Does LoopBench ranking predict downstream agent success, map consistency, or human judgments in large branching environments?
Can a fully constant-memory writer retain recoverable residual traces after landmark eviction?
How do slot rank, cache size, precision, and model training horizon interact across substantially different RoPE world-model families?
Would training with randomized slot-rank memories make the frozen-reader approximation more faithful without sacrificing short-horizon quality?

competitive_landscape.title: MemRoPE: Training-Free Infinite Video Generation via Evolving Memory Tokens
competitive_landscape.difference: MemRoPE already stores keys unrotated, applies RoPE at attention time, and compresses history into fixed dual-rate EMA tokens. WorldTrace's narrower addition is an arbitrary N-slot rank-address scheme plus distinct averaging and verbatim-recall writers and a controlled revisit benchmark; canonical storage itself is not new.

competitive_landscape.title: Infinity-RoPE: Action-Controllable Infinite Video Generation Emerges From Autoregressive Self-Rollout
competitive_landscape.difference: Infinity-RoPE uses a moving Block-Relative RoPE frame, aggressively flushes the cache to a sink and latest frame, and adds controllable temporal cuts. It targets indefinite controllable generation but does not preserve an arbitrary set of distinct compressed historical slots or explicit revisit traces.

competitive_landscape.title: WorldPack: Dynamic Frame Compression for Long-context Video World Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: WorldPack expands effective context from four to 22 frames by allocating compression according to camera pose and field-of-view overlap, and evaluates spatial recall on LoopNav. WorldTrace is geometry-free and training-free, keeps a fixed six-slot read budget at arbitrary horizon, and intervenes on RoPE addressability rather than learning a spatially aware world model.

competitive_landscape.title: RELIC: Interactive Video World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
competitive_landscape.difference: RELIC trains and distills a 14B real-time world model with camera- and action-aware compressed latent memory. WorldTrace modifies only cache reads and writes of an existing frozen checkpoint, making it much cheaper to apply but less able to learn geometry-aware retrieval or improve the generator itself.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: WorldTrace is the first training-free design to jointly keep an arbitrary number of compressed video-cache slots at distinct in-distribution positions and write their keys in canonical RoPE space, and LoopBench newly isolates return-to-scene memory. Primary prior work already provides dynamic canonical RoPE storage (MemRoPE), moving relative positions (Infinity-RoPE), compressed spatial memory (WorldPack), and trained long-horizon world-model memory (RELIC). Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is the particular slot-rank addressing rule coupled to two projection-style writers, together with a clean position-versus-content ablation and systematic self-revisit benchmark. Canonicalization, temporal compression, landmark retention, and loop consistency are not individually new, and the practical advantage is strongest for verbatim recall on a narrow pair of backbones rather than a universal long-video-memory solution.
reviewer_notes: The full 34-page text was checked, including theoretical qualifications in Appendix B, all main tables, the N=256 recall sweep, cross-architecture results, memory accounting, runtime, and author-stated limitations. Competitive descriptions were verified against primary arXiv records current through 2026-08-23. Relative improvements are labeled as relative; absolute score changes are not converted into percentages.
